entries.summary: Autosave is one setting again: the v2.01 checkbox wiring that shared the key and the Settings element id (and silently stomped the mode) is removed, the duplicate default is gone, and any boolean left in stored settings is migrated to the mode it meant.

Previewed markdown can no longer break out of image or link attributes with a quote, javascript:/data:/vbscript: links render as inert text, and the update-check links only accept http(s) URLs - closing a stored-XSS hole on the origin that holds the GitHub and pair tokens.

Both servers refuse ambiguous HTTP framing: duplicate or non-numeric Content-Length and any Transfer-Encoding are hard errors, truncated bodies are refused instead of routed, header blocks may end in CRLF or a bare LF, request reads time out at 30 seconds instead of 15 minutes, and the phone server caps concurrent connections at 32.

entries.goal: Beat Cline C1-C3: Agent v2, Plan/Act, Checkpoints
entries.summary: The agent grows up, still fully offline. Act mode now runs up to 50 steps with SEARCH, LIST, patch EDITs (not just whole-file rewrites), approval-gated terminal RUNs, and staged DELETEs, with syntax checks fed back automatically and a live plan list that survives a restart. Plan mode researches read-only and hands you a written plan; nothing is edited until you tap Act on this plan. Checkpoints snapshot the staged work after every change so review can roll back to any step, and an undo point is saved to .ghostide/checkpoints before every approved apply.

Restore counts the whole archive before touching disk (directories included) and refuses when free space cannot hold it; backup create refuses a write the disk cannot finish; the restore preview counts streamed bytes instead of trusting zip headers; duplicate entries are refused during the scan; envelope fields are validated before the password KDF runs.

Restores now keep a small write-ahead journal next to the staging area. If the app or server is killed halfway through applying a backup, the next start quietly rolls every touched file back to its pre-restore state before serving anything, instead of leaving a half-applied tree. Apply targets are also containment-checked, so a restored file cannot be carried outside the workspace by a pre-existing symlink folder.

Guest tokens now expire 12 hours after issue, and the host can revoke every guest at once from the pair panel (Revoke all guests). Expired or revoked guests are simply asked for the code again. This also closes a race in the join limiter, where parallel wrong codes could lose count against the lockout.

The second hardening marathon closes: pairing rate limits and guest roles, component-aware path containment, backup inspect and provenance, askpass and path hygiene, three more server splits, honest release tooling, and CI that keeps its own evidence - every round gated, both repos in step, and the second external audit's named items closed or plainly documented as open (LAN traffic is still unencrypted; see PAIRING.md). What remains is the device pass, which is yours: DEVICE_PASS_V231 lists the taps.

Documentation round: the hardening plan now records what actually shipped for every audit item (including the two honest deviations: CI compiles rather than assembles, and the release APK is hash-pinned in the notes because the automation credential cannot upload assets), PAIRING.md matches the rate limit and guest roles, and BUILDING.md documents what CI proves. No app code changes.

entries.goal: Do not lose the answer to a stray reload
entries.summary: While an answer is streaming, a page reload or close now triggers the browser's leave warning instead of silently discarding the in-flight answer, wherever the platform surfaces that event (desktop browsers and WebView reloads; an Android app swipe-close does not surface it). The guard keys on the same stream state as the Stop button, so it never fires when nothing is running.

The About panel now ends with a build-evidence line read live from the host: which backup formats it reads, whether pairing is required for other devices, and on Android the target SDK. It is the audit's publish-your-evidence idea at app scale: what the build claims, it shows from the running server, not from a label.

New backups carry provenance in the envelope: createdBy and the exact app version that wrote them, on both builds. Readers stay tolerant, older backups restore exactly as before, and the restore preview now shows the version that made the backup when it is there. The server also keeps its version in one named constant now, so the health reply, update check, and backup meta can never drift apart.

The audit flagged string-prefix path checks in the archive extraction code: a sibling folder whose name merely starts with the workspace name would pass. Every containment check in the Android build (workspace safe-path, eco bundle, Python runtime, git templates) now goes through one tested helper that requires a real path boundary, with a JVM truth table in CI including the sibling-prefix case. The share provider and backup service already did it this way; the desktop server uses path components throughout.

entries.goal: Control characters do not belong in paths
entries.summary: Path hygiene at the choke points: both servers now refuse any file path containing C0 control characters or DEL, before the path is resolved, while ordinary unicode names keep working. It closes a class of log-forging and terminal-escape tricks through crafted filenames, and the live probes prove refusal and the unicode case side by side.

Settings and profile imports now carry an adversarial test in the gate set: unknown keys dropped, wrong types dropped, nested objects refused, prototype-pollution attempts neutralized. The one gap the test found is fixed in this build: imported string values are capped at 20000 characters, so an import file cannot smuggle a payload in as a setting.

Pairing is no longer all-or-nothing. The host can flip a switch in the pair panel so new guests join as view-only: their token can read and send presence, and every other change is refused with a clear view-only message. Roles are set by the host at join time, shown in the guest's pair panel, and the rate limit from v2.12 still guards the code. PAIRING.md documents the model.

entries.goal: Settings search points at the answer
entries.summary: The settings filter now highlights every matching row in the studio violet instead of only hiding the rest, and pressing Enter in the search box jumps straight to the first match. Small, but settings is long now and finding one toggle should not be a scroll hunt.

No app changes in this build. The continuous-integration probes job now saves its full logs (and the GitHub-connect server logs) as a downloadable artifact whenever a run fails, so a red run explains itself inside GitHub instead of needing a local rerun to diagnose. The last four CI runs on main are green.

entries.goal: Release tooling tells the right date
entries.summary: Housekeeping with teeth: the in-app changelog generator stamped every entry with a fixed date, so a day of releases all claimed the same day. It now uses the real build date, the twelve entries it had mis-stamped were corrected, and commit messages again name the version they carry.

entries.goal: Health tells the truth about the host
entries.summary: The health endpoint on both builds now reports pairRequired, the backup formats it can read (v1 and v2), and on Android the target SDK, so any client can see what it is talking to. The pair panel uses it: a line under the pairing code shows the host build, whether pairing is required for other devices, and the backup formats supported.

Restoring a backup now previews before it confirms: enter the passphrase and the confirm dialog shows the backup's creation date, file count, size, and format version, all validated by the new inspect endpoint without changing a file. A wrong passphrase or a damaged backup is refused at the preview, before anything is overwritten.

entries.goal: Backup inspect: preview before you restore
entries.summary: New /api/backup/inspect on both builds: decrypts a backup and validates its whole manifest (entry rules, duplicates, size caps) WITHOUT changing a single file, returning its format version, file count, total bytes, and creation time. Restores also gained adversarial coverage: symlink entries land as plain files, and a truncated backup is refused cleanly.

entries.goal: BackupService: backups leave the server class
entries.summary: Internal split, no behavior change: backup create and the staged restore moved from IdeServer into a dedicated BackupService (ZIP assembly, envelope calls, ZipGuard staging and rollback), the third step of the server split after GitSupport and PairHub. One quiet improvement rides along: the restore path check is now component-aware instead of a string-prefix match. JVM backup suites pass unchanged.

entries.goal: PairHub: pair state leaves the server class
entries.summary: Internal split, no behavior change: pair presence, the pairing code, guest tokens, and the join rate limiter moved from IdeServer into a dedicated PairHub class, the second step of the server split after GitSupport. The heartbeat, peers, join, and gate call sites are unchanged in shape, and the pair probe suite passes unchanged.

The pair panel now says plainly whether this device holds a pair token for the host, and a paired guest can unpair with one tap, which forgets the stored token on this device. The host code line stays as before. Unpairing is per device; restarting the host still revokes every guest at once.

GitHub connect hardening: the desktop askpass helper now lives in a per-process unique temp file created owner-only, instead of a predictable shared temp path that another process could have planted first; the script itself never contains the token, it reads it from the environment at push time. The Android askpass file is explicitly owner-only inside the app sandbox.

Pair mode hardening: after 5 wrong pairing-code attempts from one device, joins from that device are locked for 10 minutes (the host answers 429), and a successful join clears the counter. The code itself still rotates on every server start. PAIRING.md documents the limit.

entries.goal: Hardening, round two: staged restores, pair codes, reproducible build
entries.summary: Backup restore is now staged and atomic: entries are unpacked to a staging area under strict rules (size and count caps, duplicate and traversal checks) and only applied once the whole backup validates, with rollback if anything fails mid-apply, so a hostile or damaged backup changes nothing. Pair mode gains a trust step: the host shows a fresh 6-digit code each boot and other devices enter it once to pair; loopback needs none. Under the hood: the Android build is now reproducible from a documented clean checkout, and the bundled-git code moved into its own GitSupport class.

GhostIDE now targets API 36, the level Google Play requires for new apps and updates from August 31, 2026, while still running on everything down to Android 7 (API 24). Built with the API 36 platform and build-tools. No feature changes in this build; it carries the v2.09 hardening (AES-GCM backups, request and KDF bounds) plus everything before it. On-device behavior under the new target is part of the current device pass.

entries.goal: Hardening pass: AES-GCM backups, request and KDF bounds
entries.summary: Backups are now encrypted with standard AES-256-GCM instead of the old custom construction, with hostile-file protections: KDF iteration counts and field sizes in a backup file are validated before any work is done, on both the new format and old v1 backups (which still restore). The local server now caps request bodies at 64 MB on both builds, and Android-managed backup of app data is turned off so workspaces and tokens never leave through OS backup; the in-app encrypted backup is the supported path.

entries.goal: GitHub connect: clone, pull and push from the phone
entries.summary: The git panel grows a GitHub / remote section: paste a personal access token (kept only on this device), save the origin remote, and Clone, Fetch, Pull or Push without leaving the app. The token is passed to git through a private askpass helper and is never written into .git/config. First push sets the upstream automatically.

Tools gains About this build: the version, your on-device library counts, and the latest change, in one message. This build closes batch 5: chat wrap, text-size quick buttons, search all chats (the 2.0 milestone), editor autosave, summarize chat, duplicate file, jump to latest, clear all chats, and speak last answer.
Chat options gains Speak last answer: one tap reads the newest answer aloud through the same speech path as the per-message Speak button. Tap again while it is speaking to stop.

entries.goal: Clear all chats in this project
entries.summary: Settings gains a Clear all chats button for the current project: one confirmed action deletes every chat's stored history in the project. Settings, prompts, profiles and other projects are untouched.
When you scroll up in the chat, a Latest button appears under the messages: one tap takes you back to the newest message. It hides itself when you are already at the bottom.
The header gains a Duplicate button for the open file: it suggests a name (the same name with ' copy' before the extension), copies the saved content to it, and opens the copy.

Chat options gains Summarize chat: it sends a standing instruction through the normal send path and the model recaps the conversation in at most 5 bullets: the goal, the decisions, and what is still open.

Settings gains an Autosave toggle: when on, a file with unsaved changes saves itself after about 3 seconds without typing, through the normal save path (trim-on-save and pair guards included). Off by default.

GhostIDE 2.0: Tools gains Search all chats. One query scans every chat in the project and prints the matches in place, each with its chat name, who said it, and an excerpt around the match (capped at 12 so a common word cannot flood the chat).
The chat header gains A- and A+ buttons that step the chat text size (12, 13, 15) without opening Settings. The Settings picker stays in sync.
Settings gains Wrap long lines in chat: long answers and code blocks wrap softly instead of scrolling sideways. Off by default, so nothing changes until you turn it on.

Settings tools gains an info line: the running version plus live counts of your chats, prompts, profiles and starred answers on this device. This build closes batch 4: file header actions, line operations, chat auto-name, starred sessions, What Ghost sees, starred answers, five more slash commands, retry last message, and the tabs pack.
Two buttons join the tab bar: Close others and Close all tabs. Both ride the existing close logic, so a tab with unsaved changes still asks before it closes.
Chat options gains Retry last message: when a send fails and your message is left unanswered at the end of the chat, one tap removes it and sends it again, with no duplicate in the history.
Five more slash commands: /rename (with a name), /star, /scratch, /backup and /sees. The command list is now thirteen strong and /help shows them all.
Every answer gains a Star button. Starred answers are kept in one list (up to 50) and Tools gains a Starred answers entry that shows the ten most recent in the chat.

Chat options gains a What Ghost sees button: the answer style, persona, your custom instructions, sampling settings and context budget that shape the next reply, shown as a plain system message. Display only, it never enters the conversation or the model's context.

Star chat pins a chat to the top of the picker with a star. Also fixed before it ever reached a phone: the v1.90 auto-name called session helpers that do not exist (it would have broken sending), and the v1.86 prompt export called a missing loader. Both now use the real plumbing, with a regression check that fails if the dead names come back.
A chat that still has its default name renames itself from its first message (first 28 characters). Chats you renamed yourself are never touched.
The status bar gains line operations for the editor: duplicate line, move line up or down, delete line. Inside the editor, Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the line and Alt+D duplicates it.
Two new header buttons for the open file: copy its path, or copy its full current content (unsaved edits included, since it copies the live editor buffer).

After an update, the chat quietly shows one system message naming the newest change (this one, the first time you open the new build). First installs set the baseline silently, and only the single newest entry is ever shown.
Tools gains Export all chats: every chat in the project, each titled with its name, in one Markdown file. The prompt library gains an Export prompts button that downloads it as JSON.

Chat options gains a Last run line: the latest answer's time, token and speed estimates plus the temperature and token cap that produced them. It persists across restarts instead of flashing in the context meter and vanishing.

Settings gains a Compact density toggle (tighter buttons, messages and header across the UI) and a Chat font picker (Default, System sans, Monospace, Serif) applied through a CSS variable, like the chat text size.
Tools gains a Scratchpad: one persistent note that saves itself as you type on this device. Send to chat drops it into the message box, Save as file writes it to scratchpad.md in the workspace.

Pin the open file from Chat options and it rides along on every send in that project (up to 3 pins, shown as chips, tap a chip to unpin). Pins are per project and join the same attached list as @mentions and the selection.

Save your whole setup as a named profile in Settings (style, accent, sounds, sizes, everything), then switch setups with Apply. Profiles are validated through the same strict sanitize as settings import, and applying one reloads the app with the new setup.

Chats can be duplicated: a Duplicate button copies the current chat (history included) as a new chat named with copy appended, and switches to it. The chat picker now shows a message count next to each chat name.

Answers gain an Insert button: the answer's code (or its full text when there is no code) lands in the editor at the cursor, replacing any selection. No file open, no insert - it tells you instead of failing.
The chat box remembers what you sent: press Up to recall previous messages (shell style), Down to walk back to your draft. The last 50 submissions are kept, de-duplicated, and survive restarts.

Settings gains an Auto-scroll toggle for the chat. On (the classic behavior) the chat always jumps to the newest message. Off, the view only follows when you are already near the bottom, so reading back through an answer is never interrupted while it streams.

Settings gains Export all data and Import backup: one JSON file with everything the app keeps locally (settings, prompts, all chats and sessions, drafts, bookmarks). Import validates the file strictly before touching anything, asks first, then reloads.

The completion ping gains a sound: Soft, Chime or Pop, synthesized in the app (no audio files), with a Test sound button in Settings. It only plays when the ping itself fires, and picking a sound previews it.

Settings gains an Accent color picker: Green (the current default), Violet, Blue, Amber, Rose or Teal. It recolors the primary buttons and highlights through one CSS variable, applies instantly, and is kept as part of your settings.

Tools gains Help & shortcuts: one tap prints a help card into the chat covering the answer styles, quick prompts, slash commands and keyboard shortcuts. It is assembled from the app's live tables, so it always matches what the app can actually do.
The status bar now shows the selection size (characters, plus lines when it spans several) and the current file's type (Python, JavaScript, Markdown and friends) next to the cursor position.

Every answer gains a Speak button: the device reads it aloud with markdown flattened (code blocks become a spoken placeholder instead of symbols). Tap again to stop. If the device has no speech engine, the button says so instead of failing silently.

Chat keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+. jumps to the chat box from anywhere, Ctrl+/ toggles Chat options, Ctrl+L clears the chat (with the usual warning), and Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down moves between chats. They stay out of the code editor's way, and a Shortcuts button in Chat options lists them all.

A Find in chat box in Chat options filters the visible messages as you type and counts the matches. It works on everything on screen (your messages, answers, system notes) and clears back to the full chat when emptied.

Every Ghost answer gains two more buttons: Save writes it to a file in the workspace, and Code copies only its code blocks. Your own messages gain Edit & resend: rewind the chat to that message, fix it, and send again (everything after it is removed, with a warning first).

Settings gains a filter box (type to find a setting, sections hide when nothing matches), Export and Import for carrying your settings between devices as JSON (import only accepts known settings with the right types), and a Reset all settings button. Chats and files are never touched.

Choose how much project context rides with each message: a context budget (Lean 3,000 to Huge 20,000 tokens, used by chat, slices, recall and convert alike), a switch for attaching the editor selection, and an opt-in switch that attaches the git diff of your uncommitted changes, capped so it cannot flood the model.

Chat appearance settings: text size (Small, Default, Large), panel width on desktop (Slim to Extra wide), message bubbles, and a toggle for the You / Ghost labels. All apply live and combine with Compact chat.

Type / in the chat box: /explain, /fix, /tests and /doc run the file quick actions (add a note after the command to steer it), /clear clears the chat, /export exports it, /regen repeats the last answer, and /help lists them all.

Export chat as Markdown, plain text, or a standalone web page (fully escaped, safe to share), copy the whole chat at once, and see a running count of messages, words and estimated tokens for the current chat in Chat options.
Editor display settings: line spacing (Tight, Normal, Roomy, Loose), font ligatures on or off, line numbers on or off, and the current-line highlight on or off. All apply live and are remembered.

Creativity (temperature) now lives in Chat options too, with one-tap Precise, Balanced and Creative presets in Settings; both sliders always agree. Answer length gains a Custom choice with your own token count, and after each answer the chat shows how long it took and its estimated speed.

Save the prompt in the chat box under a name, then reuse it in any project from Chat options: pick it, Insert, send. Prompts live on the device, can be replaced by saving the same name again, and can be deleted from the same row.

Every project can now hold several named chats. Switch between them in Chat options, start a new one, rename it, or delete it; each keeps its own history and its own unsent draft. Your existing chat stays as the first one, untouched.

The chat box grows as you type and shows a live character and estimated-token counter. An unsent message is kept as a draft for the project and restored when you come back. Every Ghost answer gains a Copy button, and a Continue button in Chat options picks up a cut-off answer where it left off.

Chat gets an answer style picker (Balanced, Teacher, Code only, Reviewer, Rubber duck), an answer length picker, quick prompt chips, and Regenerate / Copy / Export buttons in the options fold. Settings is grouped into Chat, Editor and Interface, and gains custom instructions for every chat, a history window, a send-key choice, a completion ping toggle, message time stamps, an editor font picker, compact chat and reduce motion.

The Context lab gains an Export section: the current slice is exported by GhostSlice itself into a bundle, then converted by the GhostConvert tool into AGENTS.md, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions, or a generic prompt - with every conversion loss named per format from the tool's own LOSSES.md, and the output verified by the tool before it is shown.
